text:
Priya (sales): FinCorp needs a formal capacity plan for their enterprise commit: ~2000 qps peaks for chat and embeddings, unpredictable spikes during launches. They asked about reserved GPU recommendation, autoscale behavior, prewarm, and security questionnaire answers.
Liam (solutions): Clarify cadence: are spikes scheduled or ad-hoc? sizing differs.
FinCorp PM: Mostly ad-hoc but tied to product events. baseline ~120 rps, spikes to ~2k for 10-25m, ~10 times/month. KV cache should help for repeated prompts but many queries are unique embeddings.
Vera (eng-infra): Quick throughput mapping: redwood-llama-8b-q profile -> ~320 qps per standard node for chat at 32 tok avg. Embeddings mix reduces per-node qps; assume effective 250 qps/node mixed. For 2000 qps peak -> reserve 8 nodes for safety (2000/250=8), recommend 8 reserved for SLA-critical customers.
Liam (solutions): Provide three purchase options: full reservation, hybrid (partial reserve + autoscale), and autoscale-only. Include expected monthly commit and sample burst cost.
Vera (eng-infra): Options sketch: A) 8 reserved nodes: covers peaks, lowest p99. B) 4 reserved + autoscale to 12: lower commit, needs prewarm before big events. C) 0 reserved + autoscale: cheapest commit, higher tail latencies.
Diego (sre): Cold start & KV warmup note: starting replicas adds model init (~5-20s) + KV population time. Embeddings coldstart faster but chat suffers. Mitigations: scheduled prewarm, synthetic warm replay, lightweight warm containers.
Priya (sales): Can we include a concrete autoscale policy snippet and a prewarm command customers can run or we can run on their behalf?
Vera (eng-infra): Sure, sample policy (abbrev):
```
autoscale_policy: min_replicas: 4
target_rps_per_replica: 110
max_replicas: 12
scale_cooldown_sec: 60
prewarm_hook: /ops/prewarm --model=llama-8b-q --prefix-file=common_prefixes.txt --parallel=8 --tokens=1M
```
Prewarm one-liner:
```
./prewarm --model llama-8b-q --prefix-file common_prefixes.txt --parallel 8 --duration 300
```
Diego (sre): Add fallback: on startup failures or very high tail p99 -> route to a quantized-4bit compatible variant in-region and fire pager. Customers must accept slight output diffs in contract.
Noemi (security): Dedicated supports customer KMS, VPC peering and per-tenant audit logs. Standard audit retention 90d, enterprise add-on for longer. I'll answer SOC2/KMS rotation/egress items in their questionnaire by EOD.
Priya (sales): Pricing calc sample needed: show committed monthly cost vs expected burst costs assuming 10 spikes/month. Use conservative per-node min cost $X/hr for back-of-envelope.
Vera (eng-infra): Back-of-envelope: extra node cost ~0.14$/min. A 20m spike that requires +6 nodes -> 6*0.14*20 = $33.6 per spike. At 10 spikes -> $336/mo burst. Reserved 8 nodes monthly = $BASE_COMMIT (we'll fill exact). Hybrid: reserve 4 nodes + burst burn estimated ~ $168/mo in same scenario.
FinCorp PM: We want AZ spread and an explicit fallback model clause in the SOW. Also need to confirm KV warmup guarantees for scheduled events.
Diego (sre): Guarantee approach: for scheduled events we can offer a prewarm SLA (run prewarm 5-10m before window). For ad-hoc spikes we recommend higher reserved baseline or accept fallback model behavior for initial minutes.
Liam (solutions): Action items: (1) Vera to run perf sim with FinCorp trace and produce numbers for A/B/C; (2) Diego to draft prewarm + fallback runbook; (3) Noemi to complete questionnaire answers; (4) Priya to draft SOW language for AZ spread and fallback acceptance.
build-bot: perf-sim job 1747654350 completed (status: success)
Vera (eng-infra): Uploaded sim summary: Option A (8 reserved) = $BASE_A/mo, median latency 95ms, p99 320ms. Option B (4 reserved + autoscale) = $BASE_B/mo + ~$336/mo sample burst, median 140ms, p99 680ms. Option C (autoscale-only) = $BASE_C/mo, median 220ms, p99 1.9s. Detailed CSV in shared drive.
Priya (sales): Great. I'll assemble customer slides with the three options and attach security answers. Setting status -> waiting_on_customer for signed schedule and traffic trace.
FinCorp PM: Thanks all. We'll review and return with preferred option and signed schedule next week.
